instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express or convey—positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the dominant feeling the tweet conveys, including mood about plans (excitement = positive; missing out, disappointment, annoyance = negative). Insults, profanity aimed at a target, sarcasm and bad news (violence, delays, failures) count as negative even when phrased factually. Announcements of products, events or achievements often read as mildly positive; plain questions, logistics, sales offers and news without evaluation are neutral, as are mixed or jokey complaints with no clear dominant feeling.

neutral.what: Informational, logistical or question tweets with no clear evaluation; news headlines, ticket sales, invitations without emotion, or ambivalent/joking remarks.
examples: Who going with me to Knott's Saturday?
Selling 2 tickets to madonna's sept 10 show. Let me know if you're interested
envy everyone going to the Big Bang shows tomorrow and Saturday. ;_;
neutral.cues: questions, may, tomorrow plans, preview, register, selling, RT news, hi can you
neutral.not_for: News describing violence, delays or failure (negative); event promotions with enthusiastic wording (positive).

positive.what: Tweets showing excitement, enjoyment, praise, pride, gratitude, hope, or upbeat promotion of events, products and achievements.
examples: If I end up going to Disneyland tomorrow I'll be the happiest girl on this planet
Congrats to Aiden Wagner who scored his 1st BCHL goal in his 1st preseason game vs. Prince George. He was named the game's 3rd star.
Tomorrow, Apple Inc. will introduce the 6S, a new Apple TV and the iPad Pro.
positive.cues: love, can't wait, so excited, happiest, congrats, great, terrific, bless, proud, favorite, wish me luck, come see
positive.not_for: Excitement undercut by inability to attend (negative); envy of others going (neutral); neutral logistics about future plans (neutral).

negative.what: Tweets expressing anger, disappointment, sadness, contempt, mockery or criticism, or reporting harmful/bad events.
examples: Sucks i cant go to the Nekromantix show OR the Brian Setzer Orchestra show tomorrow and saturday:( i really want to go:,(
Buses in the White Hart Lane & High Road N17 area may be subject to diversion & delays due to Tottenham Hotspur match
@user If you watch Any Given Sunday backwards\u002c it\u2019s like Tim Tebow\u2019s career.
negative.cues: sucks, can't go, :(, fuck, shit, worst, stupid, ugly, disappointed, bored, hell, evil, racist, fails
negative.not_for: Mild complaints framed as jokes or questions (neutral); profanity used playfully alongside excitement (positive).
